chunks: First: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mayamari, from Aban, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

"Ten men killed one man." He said: "If the heirs wish, they can kill them all, and they pay nine blood-wits (diyas). If they wish, they can choose one man and kill him, and the remaining nine pay the heir of the last killed man one-tenth of the blood-wit each, each man from them. Then the ruler disciplines them and imprisons them."
Second: From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Muskhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding two men who killed one man, he said: "If the heirs of the killed man wish to kill them both, they pay a complete blood-wit and kill them both, and the blood-wit is shared between the heirs of the two killed men. If they wish to kill one of them, they kill him, and the remaining one pays half the blood-wit to the heirs of the killed man. If they do not pay the blood-wit of one of them and one of them is not killed, they accept the blood-wit of their companion from both of them. If the heirs accept the blood-wit, it is upon both of them."
Third: Yunus, from Ibn Muskhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He said: "If two or three men kill one man and wish to kill them, they return the surplus of the blood-wit. If the heirs accept the blood-wit, it is upon them. Otherwise, they take the blood-wit of their companion."
Fourth: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding ten men who participated in killing one man, he said: "The heirs of the killed man choose, and whomever they wish they kill, and his heirs return upon the remaining nine for nine-tenths of the blood-wit."
Fifth: As for what al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Qasim ibn Urwa, from al-Abbas and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He said: "When a group gathers to kill one man, the ruler rules that whomever they wish be killed, and they are not allowed to kill more than one. Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: 'He who is killed unjustly, We have given his heir authority, so let him not exceed limits in killing.' And if three men kill one, the ruler is given the choice of which of the three to kill, and the other two guarantee two-thirds of the blood-wit for the heirs of the killed man. This does not contradict the earlier reports, because the meaning of this report is that we carry it on one of two bases: one is that we carry it on Taqiyya (dissimulation), because among the jurists is one who permits that. The other is that we carry it on the basis that he is not allowed to do that except on condition that he returns what is surplus from the blood-wit of his companion. This is contrary to what some of the common people go for, and it is the opinion of some who preceded Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), because he permitted the killing of the two and what exceeded them by one and did not return the surplus of that. And that is not permissible in any case, and that which confirms what we have presented."
Sixth: What al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Binti Ilyas narrated from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding two men who killed one man, he said: "They are killed if the heirs of the killed man wish, and one blood-wit is returned to them."

Seventh: As for what Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from some of our companions, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Abu Jumayla, from Isma'il ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a slave and a free man who killed a free man, he said: "If he wishes, he kills the free man, and if he wishes, he kills the slave. If he chooses to kill the free man, he strikes the sides of the slave. His saying: 'He strikes the sides of the slave' does not indicate that it is not obligatory upon his master to return to the heirs of the second killed man half the blood-wit or to hand over the slave to them, because if he were free, that would be upon him as we clarified. So the ruling of the slave is his ruling equally, and only discipline (ta'zir) is obligatory upon him along with that, as it is obligatory upon the free men, as narrated by al-Fudayl ibn Yasar in the report we presented earlier."
ai.seo_question: What are the Islamic legal rules for Qisas and Diya when multiple people kill one person?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi synthesizes these narrations to clarify the jurisprudential debate between the permissibility of killing multiple co-perpetrators versus selecting only one, emphasizing the ruler's (al-Wali) authority to enforce either option. The text highlights the principle of 'Taqiyya' (dissimulation) to reconcile apparent contradictions in the reports and underscores the financial liability (Diya) of the remaining perpetrators if only one is executed. This reflects the Shia emphasis on the ruler's discretion in balancing retribution with equitable compensation among the heirs.
